stories.title: Value-Add Golden Hill Apartments Trade in 1031 Exchange
stories.excerpt: Whitewater Commercial Real Estate, a San Diego-based commercial real estate brokerage specializing in multifamily, arranged the sale of 3013 C St., a value-add complex in Golden Hill. The property sold for $5,337,276. Cole Silverman, Connor Stolle and Carson Trujillo of Whitewater represented the seller, Stephanie Ranum, and the buyer, Pfeiffer Properties, LLC. “Golden Hill continues to be one of San Diego’s most desirable urban rental markets, driven by its central location, strong renter demand, and proximity to Downtown, Balboa Park, and surrounding neighborhoods,” said Silverman. “Town Pines offered the buyer an opportunity to acquire a well-located multifamily asset with strong existing fundamentals and meaningful long-term value-add potential.” The 22-unit property was built in 1985 and features a mix of one- and two-bedroom apartments, 33 secure ground-level gated parking spaces, and onsite laundry. It was acquired by a 1031 exchange buyer and offers additional upside through below-market in-place rents and strategic interior renovations. The post Value-Add Golden Hill Apartments Trade in 1031 Exchange appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pfeiffer Properties acquired 22-unit Golden Hill complex, San Diego, for $5.3M via 1031 exchange.
Value-add play: below-market in-place rents and interior renovation upside identified.
Golden Hill cited as desirable urban rental market with strong renter demand.
stories.summary: A 22-unit, 1985-built apartment complex in San Diego's Golden Hill neighborhood traded for $5.3 million to a 1031 exchange buyer. The property features mixed one- and two-bedroom units with 33 parking spaces and onsite laundry. The buyer is positioned to capture value through below-market rents and strategic interior renovations in a neighborhood cited for strong renter demand and central location near Downtown and Balboa Park.
stories.impact: Golden Hill's continued desirability signals sustained rental demand in San Diego's urban core. For developers, this validates the submarket's fundamentals and suggests room for value-add repositioning. The 1031 exchange activity also indicates capital recycling from mature assets into repositioning opportunities, a signal of healthy transaction velocity and investor confidence in the market.

stories.title: $20M Project to Add Hotel, Residential Units at Liberty Center in Ohio
stories.excerpt: Liberty Center, a 64-acre mixed-use property in Liberty Township, Ohio, announced more than $20 million in completed, ongoing and planned investments designed to support the mixed-use destination’s next phase of growth, including future hotel and residential development opportunities. Real estate developer Centennial, powered by Lincoln, serves as the asset manager for the Apollo-owned property and leads the strategic direction and execution of the initiatives. The investment spans the property’s campus and includes major tenant upgrades, first-to-market entertainment concepts, and long-term initiatives. Current plans envision approximately 300 apartment units and a full-service hotel that would complement Liberty Center’s existing mix of retail, dining, entertainment and community gathering spaces. “The investments taking place across Liberty Center reflect a long-term commitment to enhancing the customer experience, strengthening the property’s competitive position and creating sustainable value for ownership,” said Jonathan Maher, Senior Vice President of Asset Management for Centennial. The post $20M Project to Add Hotel, Residential Units at Liberty Center in Ohio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Liberty Center, Liberty Township, Ohio, planning ~300 apartment units and full-service hotel.
$20M+ invested across completed, ongoing, and planned initiatives by Apollo/Centennial.
Mixed-use destination expanding residential and hospitality to complement retail and dining.
stories.summary: Liberty Center, a 64-acre mixed-use property in Liberty Township, Ohio, is undergoing $20+ million in capital improvements, with plans for approximately 300 new apartment units and a full-service hotel. Centennial (powered by Lincoln) manages the Apollo-owned asset and is directing strategic initiatives that span tenant upgrades, entertainment concepts, and long-term residential and hospitality development.
stories.impact: The 300-unit residential component signals strong confidence in Liberty Township's demand fundamentals and the viability of mixed-use, destination-oriented development. For competitors in the Columbus metro, this represents meaningful new multifamily supply coming online; early entitlement and feasibility work on nearby sites should factor in this competitive pipeline and the submarket's growing live-work-play positioning.

stories.title: Newmark Arranges Fannie Mae Loan on San Clemente Active-Adult Complex
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged a $58-million Fannie Mae loan for Everleigh San Clemente, a newly constructed 150-unit Class A active-adult (55+) apartment community in San Clemente. The Fannie Mae financing was arranged by vice chairman Lee Redmond, managing director Alec Newman and VP Nick Schroeder of Newmark on behalf of the borrower, an institutional-level joint venture. “Everleigh San Clemente represents a rare opportunity to finance a high-quality active-adult community in an exceptionally desirable coastal market,” said Redmond. “The property’s strong sponsorship, institutional-quality construction and location within a supply-constrained submarket generated significant lender interest and enabled the execution of favorable financing terms.” Completed in 2023, Everleigh San Clemente is located within one of Orange County’s most sought-after residential markets. The property is also positioned to benefit from the ongoing revitalization of the nearby Dana Point Harbor, a $600-million-plus redevelopment project to enhance one of Southern California’s premier coastal destinations, according to Newmark. The post Newmark Arranges Fannie Mae Loan on San Clemente Active-Adult Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Fannie Mae financed 150-unit Class A active-adult (55+) community, San Clemente, with $58M loan.
Everleigh San Clemente completed 2023; supply-constrained Orange County coastal submarket.
Dana Point Harbor $600M+ redevelopment nearby enhances long-term locational tailwinds.
stories.summary: Newmark arranged a $58 million Fannie Mae loan for Everleigh San Clemente, a newly built 150-unit Class A active-adult community completed in 2023. The property benefits from San Clemente's supply-constrained coastal market position and proximity to the $600+ million Dana Point Harbor revitalization, factors that generated lender interest and favorable financing terms.
stories.impact: Strong institutional financing for a new active-adult building in Orange County validates demand for age-restricted product in supply-constrained coastal submarkets. The deal signals Fannie Mae's appetite for high-quality active-adult assets and suggests pricing/underwriting remain disciplined. For developers eyeing similar coastal markets (Newport Beach, Laguna, Ventura County), this sets a benchmark for market conditions and lending appetite in the category.

stories.title: Port of Seattle Approves $2.5B Renovation for Airport Concourse
stories.excerpt: The Port of Seattle Commission has approved initial funding for a $2.5 billion renovation of Seattle-Tacoma International Airport’s S Concourse, with major construction scheduled to begin in 2027 and continue through 2034. Commissioners authorized $1.1 billion to fund the project through 2029. The commission will consider the remaining costs later. The project will modernize the S Concourse, which opened in 1973 and primarily serves international travelers. Plans call for adding 150,000 square feet, including a new upper concourse level, more dining and retail space, additional lounges and passenger amenities, and dual-level boarding at select gates. The project will be completed in multiple phases over the course of eight years. “The project will add critical seismic, structural, and building systems upgrades to improve long-term passenger circulation as well as operational efficiency,” said Port of Seattle Commission President Ryan Calkins. Infrastructure consulting firm AECOM was selected to lead the project. The post Port of Seattle Approves $2.5B Renovation for Airport Concourse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Port of Seattle approved $2.5B S Concourse renovation; construction 2027–2034.
Project adds 150K SF, dual-level boarding, dining, retail, and structural upgrades.
Eight-year phased completion; $1.1B authorized through 2029.
stories.summary: The Port of Seattle Commission authorized initial funding for a $2.5 billion renovation of Seattle-Tacoma International Airport's S Concourse, with major construction scheduled to begin in 2027 and run through 2034. The project will expand the concourse by 150,000 square feet and add passenger amenities, dining, and retail, with phased delivery over eight years.
stories.impact: This is primarily an airport and hospitality infrastructure story with limited direct impact on multifamily development. However, the eight-year construction timeline and $2.5B capital spend may have second-order effects on Seattle-area labor supply, wage pressure, and short-term housing demand for construction workers. The project's completion (2034) is too distant to materially shift near-term multifamily demand, but it reinforces Seattle's infrastructure investment and long-term growth positioning.

stories.title: Javits Center Expansion, Tech Upgrades Boosting NYC Hospitality Industry
stories.excerpt: Five years after the Javits Center underwent a $1.5 billion expansion, the Hudson Yards convention venue is continuing to expand its bandwidth to boost its events business and the adjacent New York City hospitality industry. The 3.3 million-square-foot facility recently underwent a $5 million technology upgrade enabling the Javits Center to become the first convention center in the U.S. to provide the newest wireless network, Wi-Fi 7, Commercial Observer can first report. The Wi-Fi 7 system, which debuted last month for Fanatics Fest, provides another competitive edge in attracting more conferences and events going forward, Joyce Leveston, CEO of the Javits Center, told CO. “So many people who are coming to conventions also want to feel that they can remotely connect with their workplace,” Leveston said on Wednesday, moments before the Javits Center marked its 40th anniversary with a celebration event. “You can’t do that unless you have a state-of-the-art Wi-Fi system.” The technology enhancement is just the latest effort by the Javits Center to up the ante in terms of drawing some of the biggest conferences and events to Manhattan and providing a jolt to New York City’s economy. The Javits Center estimates that its convention bookings generated more than 100,000 hotel stays in the New York City region in 2025. The expansion of the Javits Center, which debuted in May 2021, added 1.2 million square feet to the north side of the complex, including a 55,000-square-foot ballroom and a glass-enclosed sustainable rooftop pavilion touted as the largest green roof in the Northeast. The boost to New York City’s hospitality industry from new investments to the Javits Center is evident across the street at 418 11th Avenue, where a new 455-room Hilton-branded hotel is slated to open in the next three years as part of a larger mixed-use project. A 379-room Hotel Meta developed by Marx Development Group is also planned for nearby 450 11th Avenue. The added hotels by Javits
bullets: Javits Center installed $5M Wi-Fi 7 upgrade; first U.S. convention center with this tech.
Hudson Yards venue (3.3M SF) leveraging tech edge to attract larger, longer events.
Follows $1.5B expansion five years prior; continuous amenity and capacity investment.
stories.summary: The Jacob Javits Center in Hudson Yards, New York City, completed a $5 million technology upgrade to deploy Wi-Fi 7, making it the first U.S. convention center with this wireless standard. The upgrade debuted at Fanatics Fest and is intended to enhance the venue's competitive position in attracting conferences and events. This follows a $1.5 billion expansion five years prior.
stories.impact: Javits Center's continued capital investment and technology positioning bolsters NYC's convention and event-hosting competitiveness, which drives transient and extended-stay hotel demand and visitor volume. For multifamily, this indirectly supports demand from corporate relocation/expansion tied to major conference attendees and convention-related business activity in Hudson Yards and surrounding Manhattan submarkets. The spend signals sustained confidence in Manhattan's hospitality and commercial ecosystem, stabilizing demand for residential in high-visibility mixed-use neighborhoods.

stories.title: Westphal Company Lands $56M Refi for San Diego Apartments
stories.excerpt: The Westphal Company has secured $56.1 million in permanent financing for a 354-unit apartment complex in eastern San Diego County. Northmarq arranged the fixed-rate financing through the firm’s Fannie Mae platform. The nonrecourse loan carries a 10-year term with interest-only payments for the full term. Property records identify Westphal Company owns the Wintercrest Village Apartments, a garden-style community at 12002 Wintercrest Drive in Lakeside, Calif., which is an unincorporated community roughly 20 miles northeast of Downtown San Diego. The property features one- and two-bedroom apartments, along with two swimming pools and spas, outdoor courtyards, and fitness rooms. Northmarq’s Aaron Beck, Conor Freeman and Robbie Driscoll facilitated the financing, which allowed Westphal to extract equity from the property while maintaining its cash flow, according to Beck. The lender also waived all operating escrows. “With this Fannie Mae refinance, we were able to unlock trapped equity for the borrower and preserve cash flow while keeping the loan truly non-recourse with no carve-out guarantees,” Beck said in a statement. San Diego’s multifamily market stabilized in the second quarter, with vacancy holding at 5 percent and asking rents rising 0.5 percent to $2,598 per month, according to Northmarq’s second-quarter data. Investment sales slowed roughly 25 percent compared to last year, but median pricing jumped 25 percent to $415,000 per unit. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Westphal Company refinanced 354-unit Wintercrest Village, Lakeside, San Diego, with $56.1M Fannie Mae loan.
Fixed-rate 10-year term, interest-only; nonrecourse; all operating escrows waived.
Refinance unlocked equity while preserving cash flow in eastern San Diego County submarket.
stories.summary: Northmarq arranged a $56.1 million Fannie Mae permanent refinance for Westphal Company's 354-unit garden-style Wintercrest Village Apartments in Lakeside, California (eastern San Diego County). The nonrecourse loan carries a 10-year fixed-rate term with full interest-only payments and waived operating escrows, allowing the borrower to extract equity while maintaining cash flow.
stories.impact: The favorable refinance terms (10-year fixed, IO, nonrecourse, escrow waivers) signal Fannie Mae's confidence in multifamily fundamentals and credit profiles in San Diego's outlying submarkets. For developers, this indicates strong capital availability for stabilized assets and suggests that operational quality and location stability in secondary San Diego geography can attract institutional debt. The equity extraction likely redeploys capital to new development or acquisitions, supporting continued investment activity in the region.

stories.title: Cambridge Health Alliance Renews 73K-SF Lease with Combined Properties
stories.excerpt: Cambridge Health Alliance (CHA) has renewed its 73,500-square-foot lease at Combined Properties’ 195 Canal St. in Malden, MA. Under terms of the lease, CHA will continue to operate its Malden Family Medicine Center there for at least another five years. The Malden Family Medicine Center has operated at 195 Canal St. since 2007. Affiliated with both Harvard Medical School and Tufts University School of Medicine, its services include family medicine, primary care, behavioral health, nutrition, PACE, women’s health, & pharmacy. “A true asset to the Malden area public, Cambridge Health Alliance provides the highest quality of healthcare at this leading medical facility,” said Greg Regazzini, SVP and Director of Leasing for Combined Properties. “The outstanding care is complemented by this first-class property, outfitted with all the latest medical technologies.” CHA was represented by Cresa managing principal Paul Delaney and associate Carter Swaebe. The post Cambridge Health Alliance Renews 73K-SF Lease with Combined Properties appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Cambridge Health Alliance renewed 73.5K SF lease at 195 Canal Street, Malden, MA.
Lease term: five+ years; tenant operates Malden Family Medicine Center since 2007.
CHA affiliated with Harvard Medical School and Tufts University School of Medicine.
stories.summary: Cambridge Health Alliance (CHA) renewed its 73,500-square-foot lease at Combined Properties' 195 Canal Street in Malden, Massachusetts, for a term of at least five years. CHA will continue operating the Malden Family Medicine Center, affiliated with Harvard Medical School and Tufts University, offering family medicine, primary care, behavioral health, and related services.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. The lease renewal confirms medical-office demand stability in Malden but does not signal shifts in residential demand, population migration, or labor supply. No secondary effect on multifamily fundamentals is evident.

stories.title: Fortress Refinances Dania Design Center With $45M After Foreclosure Fight
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has refinanced the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, Fla., following a nasty foreclosure fight with its previous owner, New York-based billionaire Charles Cohen. City National Bank of Florida supplied a $45 million loan backing the 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex at 1855 Griffin Road, facing the I-95. In the past two years, Fortress has invested about $3 million updating the campus, which dates back to 1988. Another $3 million to $5 million of renovations are planned over the coming year. In June, it tapped Jamestown to oversee management and leasing of the mixed-use property. The move comes about five years after the Design Center lost one of its main tenants, online pet retailer Chewy, which occupied about 100,000 square feet, when it relocated to Plantation Pointe. Fortress won control of Design Center and the neighboring Le Méridien Dania Beach hotel in 2024, through a $76 million credit bid. The proceeding was part of a broader foreclosure suit with Cohen Realty Enterprises, which Charles Cohen’s father Sherman Cohen had founded in the 1950s. In 2022, the New York-based lender provided a $535 million debt package, covering several commercial properties, including Cohens’s Dania Beach assets. The billionaire also personally guaranteed a $187 million portion of the loan. A year later, Cohen defaulted, prompting Fortress to take control of the commercial real estate. The lender also went after the borrower’s personal assets, believing the commercial properties were worth less than what Cohen owed, the Wall Street Journal reported. These include a chateau and vineyard estate in the south of France, a 220-foot megayacht, and a collection of Ferraris. In response, Cohen sold off several properties in New York. In June, Cohen announced that he had paid off the full judgement. But the legal battle remains, with Cohen filing to recoup $204 million in alleged damages. bullets: Fortress Investment Group refinanced Design Center of the Americas, Dania Beach, FL, with $45M City National Bank loan.
Fortress acquired property via $76M credit bid in 2024 after foreclosure from Charles Cohen.
780K SF office/design showroom; $3M invested YTD; $3–5M more renovations planned.
stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group secured a $45 million loan from City National Bank of Florida to refinance the Design Center of the Americas in Dania Beach, a 780,000-square-foot office and design showroom complex. Fortress acquired the property through a $76 million credit bid in 2024 following a foreclosure and has invested $3 million in upgrades, with an additional $3–5 million planned for the coming year.
stories.impact: Limited impact on multifamily development. The Design Center is office/showroom-focused, and while the refinance reflects Fortress's operational confidence, it does not signal residential demand shifts or supply pipeline changes in the Dania Beach or greater South Florida market. The Chewy tenant loss (~100K SF) five years prior showed leasing volatility, but repositioning efforts are office-centric, not residential.

stories.title: Keystone Equities Provides $61M Acquisition Debt for IOS Repositioning Site in Newark
stories.excerpt: KS Group has secured $60.5 million in acquisition debt to buy a 51-acre industrial site in Newark, N.J., that will be repositioned as an industrial outdoor storage property, Commercial Observer can first report. Keystone Equities provided the debt, structured as a senior bridge loan, marking $660 million in capital the firm has deployed since August 2023, the firm noted in a release. KS Group is buying the site from an ownership group led by Daryl Hagler. CBRE’s Shlomo Weissberg and Eli Klapper arranged the transaction. Jonathan Zamir, founder and CEO of Keystone Equities, noted in a statement that the site is currently under active environmental remediation and still hadn’t secured a certificate of occupancy before closing, which led to several “traditional lenders” to decline to underwrite the risk associated with the deal. “This was a deal that required real diligence. We dug in, structured around the risks, and found a solution that works for both us and the borrower,” he said. “That’s where Keystone adds value.” Located at 151 Raymond Boulevard in Newark, the industrial site is a former PSEG property that holds proximity to Port Newark-Elizabeth and New York City. The new IOS site will include parking for both trucks and trailers, a container garage for shipping, and electric vehicle and solar charging stations. CBRE noted in recent reports that IOS vacancy in Northern New Jersey stands at 2.5 percent, while rents have grown 123 percent since 2020. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: KS Group secured $60.5M senior bridge loan (Keystone Equities) for 51-acre Newark, NJ industrial site.
Property repositioning from brownfield to industrial outdoor storage; environmental remediation ongoing.
Lender absorbed risk; no COO at close; traditional lenders declined underwriting.
stories.summary: KS Group secured $60.5 million in senior bridge debt from Keystone Equities to acquire a 51-acre industrial site at 151 Raymond Boulevard in Newark, New Jersey. The property is being repositioned as industrial outdoor storage and remains under environmental remediation without a certificate of occupancy at closing, a risk profile traditional lenders declined to underwrite.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact. The deal demonstrates robust capital availability for distressed/remediation-heavy industrial repositioning in the Newark submarket, which may signal broader confidence in Jersey City/Newark industrial revival. However, industrial outdoor storage development does not directly compete for land or capital with multifamily. No observable effect on residential demand or construction costs in Newark is implied.

stories.title: Zimmet Law Group Relocates to 5K SF at GFP’s 515 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Zimmet Law Group is relocating its practice inside Manhattan’s Plaza District. Zimmet signed a 5,476-square-foot lease for a newly completed space inside GFP Real Estate’s 515 Madison Avenue, also known as the DuMont Building. Located at the corner of East 53rd Street, the 42-story office tower is just one block south of Zimmet’s current abode in RFR Holding’s 477 Madison Avenue. Zimmet’s practice areas range widely, from matrimonial and family law to real estate matters. The law firm was represented by Savitt Partners’ Elliot Zelinger, while GFP’s Martin McGrath and Kephra Stone negotiated in-house for the landlord. Zelinger did not respond to a request for comment. Asking rent for the nearly 10-year lease term was not disclosed, but office asking rents in Midtown averaged $88.50 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to Cushman & Wakefield data. Zimmet is expected to take occupancy at 515 Madison later this year, according to GFP, following the completion of its new space. Zimmet’s office did not respond to a request for comment on the relocation. Earlier this year, GFP took full ownership of the 350,000-square-foot Class A tower after securing an $86.5 million refinancing deal with Apple Bank, which enabled the buyout of ATCO Properties & Management’s remaining 40 percent stake in the property. By late February, the landlord had secured 12,000 square feet of new leasing activity, Commercial Observer reported. GFP announced another 9,000 square feet of deals in late July, including leases for investment firm T7 Capital, aesthetic training provider Innovation Training Specialist and Widowski Law Group. Other tenants at 515 Madison include alternative asset manager Whitebox and therapy provider Manhattan Psychiatry Group. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Zimmet Law Group leased 5.5K SF at GFP Real Estate's 515 Madison Avenue, Manhattan.
Relocation within Plaza District; nine-year lease term; one block south of prior location.
Midtown office asking rents averaged $88.50/SF in Q2 2026.
stories.summary: Zimmet Law Group signed a 5,476-square-foot lease for newly completed space at 515 Madison Avenue (DuMont Building) in Manhattan's Plaza District, relocating from nearby 477 Madison Avenue. The roughly ten-year lease was negotiated by GFP's in-house team; asking rents in Midtown averaged $88.50 per square foot in Q2 2026, though specific terms were not disclosed.
stories.impact: Negligible relevance to multifamily development. A single-tenant law firm relocation within Midtown Manhattan does not signal broader office market recovery, CBD residential demand shifts, or supply-chain changes affecting apartment development. No secondary effect on multifamily capital, demand, or construction fundamentals is evident.
